name: Mech Brawl
desc: When hit in melee range, automatically counter-attack at half damage. Turns every incoming punch into a trade.
flavor: You hit me, I hit back. Simple math.
notes: The starter Striker maneuver. Available immediately with skill_combat 1 and muscle 2. Low barrier — most players can equip this in their first hour of combat. Counter-attack at 50% damage means it's always net positive when it triggers.

name: Power Strike
desc: Replace normal attack with a devastating single blow. +80% melee damage, +10 Heat generated.
flavor: The hydraulic arm winds back. The enemy sees it coming. Doesn't matter.
notes: Core melee damage amplifier. +80% is significant but not doubled — keeps it useful across the whole game without being mandatory. The heat cost (10) punishes spamming in Light frames with low heat cap (80). Requires a fight-category weapon equipped.

name: Berserker Protocol
desc: When Stress exceeds 60%, adrenaline kicks in. +20% ATK but -15% DEF. The more desperate you get, the harder you hit.
flavor: Pain is just fuel for the machine.
notes: Risk-reward instinct. Only activates when you're already in trouble (stress >60%). The DEF penalty makes you MORE likely to take damage, which generates MORE stress, which keeps the buff active. Creates a death spiral OR a comeback depending on how much HP you have left. Grit requirement ensures the pilot can handle the stress levels.

name: Pile Bunker Strike
desc: Channel all power into a single catastrophic melee blow. +150% damage, +15 Heat. The kind of hit that ends fights.
flavor: One shot. One kill. One very hot cockpit.
notes: The Striker capstone. +150% damage is massive — with a Taeyang Corona heat blade on a Leviathan (ATK 8+), this one-shots most medium parts. bonusVsBreach +50% means BREACH tokens amplify this further. The heat cost (15) is brutal — in a Light frame with heatCap 80, two Pile Bunkers push you to shutdown territory. Reflex requirement (4) represents the precision needed to deliver the blow.

name: Relentless Assault
desc: After destroying an enemy part, immediately gain a bonus attack against another part. The momentum of destruction.
flavor: The arm is gone. The leg is next. Don't stop.
notes: Snowball maneuver. Once you start destroying parts, you accelerate. The bonus attack at 60% damage prevents it from being a full free turn. Pairs devastatingly with Offensive stance (more damage = faster part kills = more procs). The ideal Striker chain: Power Strike → destroy arm → Relentless procs → hit another part.

name: Brace for Impact
desc: When hit, reduce incoming damage by 25%. The frame absorbs the blow instead of the parts.
flavor: Plant your feet. Tighten the frame. Take it.
notes: Starter Defender maneuver. 25% damage reduction on EVERY hit is enormous over a long fight. The bonus stress reduction (-1 per hit) means Defenders stay calm under fire. This is the 'I am the wall' maneuver — simple, reliable, powerful.

name: Iron Will
desc: At the start of each turn, if Stress is above 40%, reduce it by 2. The pilot masters their own fear.
flavor: Fear is a signal. You decide what to do with it.
notes: Anti-panic maneuver. -2 stress per turn counteracts Heavy frame's +0.7 stress/turn AND most crit hit stress. Keeps the pilot in Calm/Tense range longer. Pairs with Brace for Impact (reduce damage AND stress). The 'unbreakable wall' combo.

name: Emergency Repair
desc: When any part drops below 25% HP, automatically restore 15% of that part's max HP. Once per combat per part.
flavor: The nano-gel activates. It won't hold forever, but forever isn't the plan.
notes: The 'second chance' maneuver. 15% heal when a part hits critical buys 1-2 more hits before destruction. 4 uses per combat = one per part (torso, arms, legs). The neuro requirement represents the technical knowledge to jury-rig field repairs. Doesn't prevent destruction, just delays it.

name: Fortress Protocol
desc: At combat start, sacrifice 20% ATK for the entire fight. In return, gain +30% DEF and reduce all stress gains by 50%.
flavor: You're not here to kill. You're here to survive. There's a difference.
notes: The ultimate tank commitment. -20% ATK means fights last longer, but +30% DEF and -50% stress gain means you outlast anything. On a Type 90 Fortress with Kuroda parts, this creates a nearly impenetrable wall. The tradeoff: you win by attrition, not by damage. Stacks with Defensive stance for extreme durability.

name: Last Stand
desc: When the torso enters its final integrity bar, all stats receive +40% and stress is frozen for 3 turns. The pilot refuses to go down.
flavor: Grandpa's voice in the headset: 'Not yet. You don't fall yet.'
notes: The Defender capstone. Mirrors COR's 'crisis bonus' from the combat doc but amplified. +40% to everything for 3 turns is a massive comeback window. The narrative flavor connects to Grandpa — this is the family legacy activating. Requires grit 7, which means the pilot has truly mastered resilience.

name: Aimed Shot
desc: Replace normal attack with a precision shot. -30% damage but +40% accuracy and attacks the specific part you've targeted.
flavor: Patience. Breath. Squeeze.
notes: The anti-Power Strike. Less damage, more control. targetOverride means this attack always hits the part the player's targeting mode specifies — bypassing random targeting. On a Valletta sniper with +20 base accuracy, Aimed Shot becomes nearly unmissable. The Tactician's bread and butter.

name: Exploit Weakness
desc: At turn start, scan the enemy. If any part has a BREACH token, your next attack against that part deals +50% damage.
flavor: The armor is cracked. Hit it there. Hit it again.
notes: Synergy maneuver. Requires another source of BREACH tokens (weapon crits, Mark Target, etc). When it works, +50% damage on already-weakened parts creates devastating focus-fire. The Tactician doesn't create openings alone — they exploit them. Focus 3 represents the analytical ability to identify weak points.

name: Mark Target
desc: Replace attack with a targeting scan. Apply 2 TARGET LOCK and 1 BREACH to a single enemy part. Sets up everything else.
flavor: Painting the target. Everyone else does the rest.
notes: The setup maneuver. Costs a full attack action but applies 3 tokens. TARGET_LOCK improves subsequent accuracy, BREACH increases subsequent damage. In a 2-turn sequence: Mark Target → Exploit Weakness + Aimed Shot = precision devastation. Zero heat cost — purely electronic warfare.

name: System Scan
desc: At combat start, reveal the enemy's full loadout: frame, parts, weapons, and stance. Knowledge is power.
flavor: Frame: KZ-9H. Torso: Siege class. Weapons: dual ballistic. Weakness: heat management. Engaging.
notes: Information warfare. Revealing the enemy loadout lets the combat log show detailed information (which parts are weak, what weapons they carry). The +5 accuracy for the entire combat represents the tactical advantage of knowing your opponent. Pure utility — no damage, no tokens, just knowledge.

name: Suppressing Fire
desc: Replace attack with sustained fire across all enemy parts. Each part takes 40% normal damage and receives 1 SUPPRESS token (-10% accuracy for 2 turns).
flavor: Keep their heads down. Keep shooting. They can't aim if they can't think.
notes: The Tactician capstone. Hits ALL enemy parts simultaneously (4 targets × 40% damage = 160% total damage distributed). Each part gets SUPPRESS (-10% accuracy for 2 turns). Massive control tool but expensive: 12 heat, 2 supply. Requires ranged weapon. The 'battlefield control' maneuver.

name: Coolant Flush
desc: At turn start, if Heat exceeds 50%, automatically vent 15 Heat. Keeps the frame running when others shut down.
flavor: The coolant lines hiss. Steam vents from every joint. The cockpit temperature drops three degrees.
notes: The thermal management maneuver. 15 heat vented per turn when above 50% is enormous — it effectively raises the 'safe operating window' by 15 points. On a Light frame with heatCap 80, this means you can fire energy weapons almost freely. On a Heavy frame (heatCap 120), it prevents shutdown spirals. The #1 Support pick for energy weapon builds.

name: Field Patch
desc: Replace attack with emergency repairs. Restore 20% max HP to the lowest-HP part. Costs 5 Heat and 1 Supply.
flavor: Weld, patch, pray. In that order.
notes: The active heal. 20% max HP is significant — on a KZ Siege Torso (150 HP), that's 30 HP restored. Costs an attack action + supply + heat, so there's a real opportunity cost. The Support has to choose: heal now or attack now? This is the core Support decision.

name: Overclock
desc: At combat start, push all systems beyond safe parameters. +15% to all stats for the entire combat, but +0.3 stress per turn and +20% heat generation.
flavor: The warning lights turn red. All of them. You dismiss the alerts and push the throttle forward.
notes: The 'tech boost'. +15% everything sounds great until the stress and heat costs pile up. On a Light frame (stress/crit +2.0, heatCap 80), Overclock is a gamble. On a Heavy frame with Iron Will and Coolant Flush, the penalties are manageable. This is where Support and Defender synergize — one boosts, the other stabilizes.

name: Ammo Conservation
desc: Passive: all weapon supply costs reduced by 1 (minimum 0). The pilot optimizes every shot, every burst, every reload.
flavor: Three rounds where others use ten. Precision, not volume.
notes: The 'infinite grind' maneuver. Supply cost -1 means tier 1 weapons (supplyCost 1) become FREE. Combined with a Sora Courier (supply efficiency 1.3×), the player can farm indefinitely without resupply. Focus 5 requirement means this is a mid-game unlock. Changes the economic equation of combat completely.

name: Neural Override
desc: When Heat reaches critical (>75%), instead of suffering penalties, convert excess heat into bonus damage. +2% damage per heat point above 75.
flavor: The safeties are off. The neural link burns. Everything hits harder when you stop caring about tomorrow.
notes: The Support capstone. Transforms heat from a problem into an advantage. At heat 90 on a frame with heatCap 100, that's +30% damage (15 points above 75 × 2%). Combined with Taeyang weapons that generate tons of heat, this creates a 'burning' build that gets stronger as it overheats. ignoreHeatPenalties means no accuracy loss or energy cost increases at critical heat. The ultimate tech-pilot fantasy.
